subject: How to use the posterior sample obtained for parameters as prior for another model?

messages.author: 0631c9d875251b52
messages.subject: How to use the posterior sample obtained for parameters as prior for another model?
parts:
Hi Everybody,
1. Let us say I have 3 models A,B,C and I want to use posterior obtained from Model A as prior to parameters in models B and C (B and C are different stan files). One easy way is to just obtain the mean and variance of the posterior of model A and use a gaussian prior with those parameters. Is there a better way to do this?

2. Let us say I have model posterior of whose parameters are simulated via a sampling by providing data D1 after some time I obtain new data D2 can I update HMC sampling chain with new observed data D2 or should I rerun the HMC to convergence with data D1+D2 in one shot?

3. What I would also like to know is, does the sampling-chain store all the data that was used to converge it internally ? or does it summarize it in some way? My intuition says it actually stores all the data that was used to run the chain to convergence and I am just hoping my intuition is wrong as this would seriously limit how I can update the model in an online fashion. I would love to hear advice on how one would go about solving such a problem.

Thanks,
Sunil.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to use the posterior sample obtained for parameters as prior for another model?
parts:
> On Apr 7, 2015, at 2:43 PM, Sunil S Nandihalli <sunil.na...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Everybody,
> 1. Let us say I have 3 models A,B,C and I want to use posterior obtained from Model A as prior to parameters in models B and C (B and C are different stan files). One easy way is to just obtain the mean and variance of the posterior of model A and use a gaussian prior with those parameters. Is there a better way to do this?

Fit everything jointly. Everything else is an approximation.
(Though technically with M posterior draws for A, you could use
those to run M fits for B, and so on, but you'll run into
serious combinatorial problems that way.)

> 2. Let us say I have model posterior of whose parameters are simulated via a sampling by providing data D1 after some time I obtain new data D2 can I update HMC sampling chain with new observed data D2
There is no way to do that soundly.
> or should I rerun the HMC to convergence with data D1+D2 in one shot?

> 3. What I would also like to know is, does the sampling-chain store all the data that was used to converge it internally ? or does it summarize it in some way? My intuition says it actually stores all the data that was used to run the chain to convergence and I am just hoping my intuition is wrong as this would seriously limit how I can update the model in an online fashion. I would love to hear advice on how one would go about solving such a problem.

Which interface are you talking about and what do you mean by "sampling-chain"?

Stan runs MCMC in two phases:

1. a warmup phase that estimates step size and mass matrix, and

2. a sampling phase that draws from the posterior using estimated
step size and mass matrix from warmup phase.

The warmup draws do not constitute a Markov chain and shouldn't
be used for inference.

The output of all of the interfaces store the results of adaptation, but
we don't currently have a way to read those back in for a warm start. (It's
on our to-do list and we should get to it this year, we hope.)

- Bob
